examples.en: My heart pounded before the presentation.
I trembled with a racing heart waiting for the results.
It was my first date, so my heart fluttered.
I was nervous with a pounding heart before opening the letter.

examples.ko: 놀이기구를 타기 전부터 심장이 두근두근 뛰어요.
examples.en: My heart starts thumping even before I get on the ride.
I opened the gift with excited anticipation.

explain: 설레거나 긴장할 때 심장이 뛰는 소리와 느낌을 흉내 내는 말이에요. 좋은 기대와 불안 둘 다에 쓰고, '두근거리다'와 '두근두근하다'는 같은 느낌의 동사예요. '쿵쾅쿵쾅'은 더 세게 뛸 때 써요.

phrases.en: I'm so excited about tomorrow's picnic that my heart is pounding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대돼서 마음이 들뜰 때 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used together when you are excited with anticipation.
phrases.en_equiv: to feel a flutter of excitement

phrases.en: My heart is pounding, so I can't sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두근두근과 같은 느낌의 동사로, 문장에서 서술어로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb with the same feeling, used as the predicate of a sentence.

phrases.en: I was so startled that my heart pounded hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두근두근보다 더 세고 크게 뛸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the heart beats harder and louder than with 두근두근.

explain_en: It imitates the sound and feeling of a heartbeat when you are excited or nervous, and works for both happy anticipation and anxiety. 두근거리다 and 두근두근하다 are verbs with the same feel. 쿵쾅쿵쾅 is for a much harder pounding.

en: to be dry and fluffy; to be soft and dry

examples.en: The blanket dried in the sun is really soft and dry.

examples.ko: 샤워 후에 뽀송뽀송한 수건으로 닦으니 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: Wiping off with a dry, fluffy towel after a shower feels good.

examples.ko: 빨래가 뽀송뽀송해지려면 바람이 잘 통해야 해요.
examples.en: For laundry to dry nicely, the air needs to circulate well.
I want to keep my room dry even in the rainy season.
Applying powder makes my face feel smooth and dry, and I like that.

examples.ko: 건조기에서 갓 나온 옷은 늘 뽀송뽀송하네요.
examples.en: Clothes fresh out of the dryer are always nice and dry.

explain: 축축하지 않고 산뜻하게 마르면서 부드러운 느낌일 때 써요. 이불, 수건, 빨래, 피부에 자주 쓰고 반대말은 '눅눅하다, 축축하다'예요.

phrases.en: I took out a fluffy dry towel and dried my hair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 형태로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used before a noun to describe it.

phrases.en: I dried the laundry on the balcony until it was fluffy and dry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말리는 결과가 산뜻하게 되도록 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when drying something so that it ends up fresh and dry.

phrases.en: The freshly washed blanket is soft and dry.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뽀송뽀송하다'보다 순한 느낌의 같은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same word with a gentler feel than 뽀송뽀송하다.

explain_en: It is used when something is not damp but fresh, dry and soft. It often describes blankets, towels, laundry and skin, and the opposites are '눅눅하다' and '축축하다'.

t90.ax: The blanket dried in the sun is really soft and dry.

examples.en: I twisted my ankle coming down the stairs.
If you sprain something while exercising, apply ice right away.
My foot twisted and I almost fell.

examples.ko: 손목을 삐끗한 것 같아서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: I thought I had sprained my wrist, so I went to the hospital.
Go down carefully so you don't twist anything.
I may have wrenched it, because my lower back keeps hurting.

explain: '삐다, 접질리다'와 비슷하지만 '삐끗하다'는 관절이 순간적으로 살짝 어긋난 느낌이에요. 몸뿐 아니라 '계획이 삐끗하다'처럼 일이 조금 어긋날 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I twisted my ankle while playing soccer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말로, 발목이 순간 꺾였을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, used when the ankle gives way for a moment.

phrases.en: I wrenched my back lifting a heavy load.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 무리해서 허리가 살짝 상했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the back is slightly hurt by a sudden strain.

phrases.en: I fell and sprained my wrist.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삐끗하다'보다 조금 더 다친 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests a slightly more serious injury than 삐끗하다.

explain_en: It is similar to '삐다' and '접질리다', but '삐끗하다' gives the feel of a joint slipping slightly out of place for a moment. It is also used for things going slightly wrong, as in '계획이 삐끗하다'.

t90.ax: My foot twisted and I almost fell.

en: to lift; to pull up; to praise highly

examples.en: I pulled up my pants and started walking again.

examples.ko: 그는 눈썹을 추켜올리며 놀란 표정을 지었어요.
examples.en: He raised his eyebrows and looked surprised.

examples.ko: 무거운 가방을 어깨 위로 추켜올리는 모습이 힘들어 보였어요.
examples.en: Hitching the heavy bag up onto his shoulder looked tiring.
My skirt keeps slipping down, so I keep having to pull it up.

examples.ko: 안경을 코 위로 추켜올리면 잘 보여요.
examples.en: If I push my glasses up my nose, I can see well.
The jeans were too big, so I was busy pulling them up all the time.

explain: 바지, 양말, 안경, 눈썹, 어깨처럼 몸에 붙은 것을 위로 쭉 올릴 때 잘 써요. 반대로 아래로 내릴 때는 '내리다'를 써요. '추켜올려요', '추켜올렸어요'처럼 바뀌어서 어간이 달라지는 점에 주의해요.

phrases.en: He said he didn't know and shrugged his shoulders.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 한 부분을 위로 올리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for lifting a body part upward.

phrases.en: My pants keep falling, so I keep pulling them up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 현재를 나타내는 해요체 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The present-tense polite form.

phrases.en: The teacher raised their eyebrows and looked at me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷한 말이고, 둘 다 위로 쭉 올릴 때 써요. 눈썹이나 눈을 올릴 때 특히 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word; both mean to lift something up. It is especially common for eyebrows or eyes.

explain_en: Pull slipped clothing or glasses back up (안경을 추켜올리다) It's used when you pull something attached to the body upward, such as pants, socks, glasses, eyebrows or shoulders. For lowering something, you use '내리다'. Note that it changes form to '추켜올려요' and '추켜올렸어요', so the stem shape changes.

t90.ax: He raised his eyebrows and looked surprised.

examples.en: I changed into a patient gown at the hospital.

examples.ko: 환자복을 입으니 진짜 환자가 된 것 같았어요.
examples.en: Putting on the hospital gown made me feel like a real patient.
I put a cardigan over my hospital gown and went for a walk.
When I was discharged, I returned the hospital gown to the nurse.
The hospital gown was big, so I had to roll up the sleeves.

examples.ko: 환자복 차림으로 복도를 걷는 사람이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people were walking down the hall in hospital gowns.

explain: 입원했을 때 병원에서 주는 옷이에요. '환자복을 입다/갈아입다/벗다'처럼 말하고, 집에서 입는 잠옷이나 운동복과는 달라요.

phrases.en: I put on the patient gown before the surgery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입원하거나 검사받을 때 병원 옷을 입는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when wearing the hospital clothes for admission or tests.

phrases.en: I took off the patient gown on the day I left the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 퇴원할 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when leaving the hospital.
phrases.en_equiv: to take off a patient gown

phrases.en: I walked down the hallway in a patient gown.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~ 차림'은 그 옷을 입은 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '~ 차림' describes how someone looks while wearing that outfit.

explain_en: This is the clothing the hospital gives you when you are admitted. You say '환자복을 입다/갈아입다/벗다', and it is different from pajamas or sportswear worn at home.

examples.en: A small scar was left where I got hurt.

examples.ko: 남의 흉을 보는 건 나쁜 버릇이에요.
examples.en: Badmouthing other people is a bad habit.

examples.ko: 그 흉은 시간이 지나면 거의 안 보일 거예요.
examples.en: That scar will hardly be visible after some time.

examples.ko: 친구 앞에서 남의 흉만 보면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't do nothing but badmouth others in front of your friends.
Everybody has a flaw or two.

examples.ko: 수술 자국이 흉으로 남아서 신경 쓰여요.
examples.en: The surgery mark stayed as a scar, and it bothers me.

explain: '흉'은 몸에 남은 상처 자국도, 남의 부족한 점도 가리켜요. 몸의 자국은 '흉터'라고 하는 경우가 훨씬 많아요. '흉을 보다'는 없는 자리에서 남의 단점을 말하는 거라 조심해서 써야 해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람이 없을 때 모두 흉을 봤어요.
phrases.en: to badmouth someone
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 자리에 없는 사람의 단점을 말하는 거예요. 줄여서 '흉보다'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means talking about the faults of someone who isn't there. It can be shortened to '흉보다'.

explain_en: A fault to gossip about (흉을 보다); also a scar (흉이 남다), though the usual word for a scar is (흉터). '흉' can mean a mark left on the body or a fault in someone else. For a mark on the body, '흉터' is used much more often. '흉을 보다' means talking about someone's faults when they are not there, so use it carefully.

t90.ax: Everybody has a flaw or two.

examples.en: The child laughs happily riding the wooden horse.
There is an old wooden horse at the playground.
Do you know the story of the Trojan horse?
My younger sibling rocked back and forth on the rocking horse.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 손자에게 나무 목마를 만들어 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandpa made a wooden toy horse for his grandson.
This rocking horse has been here since I was a baby.

explain: 목마는 말 모양 장난감이나 놀이기구 말에 써요. 아이를 어깨에 태우는 '목말'과 소리가 비슷해서 헷갈리지만 서로 다른 말이에요. '트로이 목마'는 컴퓨터 바이러스 이야기에도 나와요.

phrases.en: A child rides the wooden horse at the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탈것이나 놀이기구를 말할 때 '타다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 타다 for rides and toys.

phrases.en: We rode the merry-go-round at the amusement park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빙글빙글 도는 놀이기구를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spinning amusement park ride.

phrases.en: My grandfather made me a wooden horse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무로 만든 말 모양 장난감을 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A horse-shaped toy made of wood.

explain_en: 목마 refers to a toy horse or a ride horse. It sounds close to 목말 (carrying a child on the shoulders), but they are different words. 트로이 목마 also appears in talk about computer viruses.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 후반에 두 골을 실점했어요.
examples.en: Our team conceded two goals in the second half.
The defense wobbled and we ended up conceding.
Everyone fell back so as not to concede.
Every time we conceded, the coach called a timeout.
If you concede first, it is hard to turn the game around.
The pitcher who gave up runs in a row was replaced.

explain: '득점하다'와 짝을 이루는 스포츠 말이에요. 축구나 야구 중계에서 '실점 없이 막았다'처럼 자주 들려요. 일상에서는 '점수를 내주다'라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀은 한 경기도 실점하지 않았어요.
phrases.en: Our team did not concede in a single game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 수비가 잘됐다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form shows the defense did well.

phrases.en: We conceded first, so I was worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기에서 상대보다 먼저 점수를 내줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a team gives up the first point.

phrases.en: We gave up a point at the end and lost.
phrases.nuance_ko: '실점하다'를 일상 말로 풀어서 한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain everyday way to say 실점하다.

explain_en: This is the sports pair of '득점하다' (to score). You often hear it in soccer and baseball broadcasts, as in '실점 없이 막았다'. In casual talk people also say '점수를 내주다'.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 마지막에 극적인 역전승을 거뒀어요.
examples.en: Our team scored a dramatic comeback win at the end.
Yesterday's game was a comeback win, so it was even more fun.

examples.ko: 두 골 뒤지다가 역전승을 하다니 믿기지 않아요.
examples.en: I can't believe they won from two goals behind.
Everyone was happy to hear the comeback news.
The coach said the secret to the comeback was stamina.
In baseball, comeback wins excite fans the most.

explain: 역전승은 지고 있다가 뒤집어서 이긴 경기예요. 반대는 '역전패'이고, 처음부터 크게 이기는 것은 '압승'이에요. 보통 '역전승을 거두다'나 '역전승을 하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: Our team won a comeback victory in the second half.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'를 붙여 이야기하듯 편하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 makes it sound casual and conversational.

phrases.en: The players gave their all and won a comeback victory.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거두다'는 '하다'보다 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 거두다 is used more in news and writing than 하다.

phrases.en: Everyone shouted at the thrilling comeback win.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기쁘고 놀라운 느낌을 더할 때 '짜릿한'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 짜릿한 to show a thrilled, surprised feeling.

explain_en: 역전승 is a win after trailing. Its opposite is 역전패, and winning big from the start is 압승. It usually appears as 역전승을 거두다 or 역전승을 하다.

examples.en: The mermaid in the fairy tale lives in the sea.
Do you know the story of the little mermaid?
The child sleeps holding a mermaid doll.
I want to swim as well as a mermaid.
A mermaid statue stands at the beach.
I watched a movie where a mermaid becomes a human.

explain: 대부분 동화 '인어공주'로 접하는 말이에요. 수영을 아주 잘하는 사람을 '인어 같다'고 비유하기도 해요. 가장 흔한 짝말은 '인어공주', '인어 동상'이에요.

phrases.en: The story of the Little Mermaid is very famous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing.

phrases.en: There is a mermaid statue by the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동상으로 만든 인어를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A mermaid made as a statue.

phrases.en: That swimmer is like a mermaid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수영을 아주 잘하는 사람을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for an excellent swimmer.

explain_en: Most people meet this word through the fairy tale '인어공주' (The Little Mermaid). Someone who swims very well can be called '인어 같다'. Common pairings are '인어공주' and '인어 동상'.

en: fastball; straight pitch; direct overseas purchase

examples.ko: 저는 인터넷으로 해외 직구를 자주 해요.
examples.en: I often buy things directly from overseas online.
The clothes I bought directly from abroad arrived in a week.

examples.ko: 직구는 배송비와 세금을 꼭 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: With overseas purchases you must check the shipping fee and taxes.
That pitcher's fastball is very quick.

examples.ko: 감독은 변화구 대신 직구로 승부하라고 했어요.
examples.en: The manager said to go with the fastball instead of breaking balls.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 말을 돌리지 않고 직구로 말해요.
examples.en: That friend speaks straight, without beating around the bush.

explain: 쇼핑 이야기에서는 해외 사이트에서 직접 사는 것이고, 야구에서는 휘지 않고 곧게 오는 빠른 공이에요. 야구에서 반대는 '변화구'예요. 쇼핑은 '직구하다'로도 말해요. 대화에서 '직구로 말하다'처럼 비유로도 써요.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 항상 직구로 말해서 편해요.
phrases.en: to speak frankly
phrases.nuance_ko: 야구의 직구처럼 변화구 없이 곧바로 말한다는 뜻이에요. 돌려 말하지 않아서 솔직하다는 칭찬으로도, 너무 직접적이라는 뜻으로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like a fastball with no breaking pitch, you say it straight. It can be praise for being honest or a hint that someone is too direct.

explain_en: Baseball: a straight pitch with no break; also direct buying from overseas online stores (해외 직구) In shopping talk, 직구 means buying directly from overseas sites, and in baseball it is the fast ball that flies straight. In baseball its opposite is 변화구 (breaking ball). For shopping you can also say 직구하다. It is also used figuratively, as in 직구로 말하다.

examples.en: A friend sang a congratulatory song at the wedding.
Who is going to sing the celebration song?

examples.ko: 축가 연습을 매일 저녁에 하고 있어요.
examples.en: I practice the celebration song every evening.
Which song should we choose for the celebration?
The song lifted the whole mood.
The song at my sibling's wedding was so moving.

explain: 결혼식에서 가장 많이 들어요. 보통 친구나 가수가 신랑 신부를 위해 부르고 '축가를 부르다'로 같이 써요. 생일에 부르는 노래는 '축가'보다 '생일 노래'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 제 결혼식에서 친구가 축가를 불러 줬어요.
phrases.en: A friend sang a congratulatory song at my wedding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말로, 결혼식 노래를 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for singing at a wedding.

phrases.en: I asked my friend to sing at the wedding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼식에서 노래할 사람에게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking someone to sing at a wedding.
phrases.en_equiv: to ask someone to sing at a wedding

phrases.en: Which song would be good for a wedding?
phrases.nuance_ko: '축가'가 어떤 자리의 노래인지 분명하게 말해 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear which occasion the song is for.

explain_en: Song sung to celebrate, typically at a wedding. You hear it mostly at weddings, where a friend or singer performs for the couple. It pairs with 부르다: '축가를 부르다'. For a birthday, people say 생일 노래 rather than 축가.

examples.en: Let us suppose it is raining.

examples.ko: 내가 부자라고 가정하면 뭘 할 거예요?
examples.en: If you suppose I am rich, what would you do?
The teacher assumed a problem situation.
I prepare by assuming the worst case.
What is the reason you assumed that?
First I will assume I fail the exam.

explain: 사실인지 모르지만 일단 그렇다고 치고 생각할 때 써요. '만약'이나 '-다면'과 비슷하지만, '가정하다'는 생각의 출발점을 정하는 말이에요. 명사 '가정'은 '가족'이나 '집'의 뜻도 있어서 헷갈리기 쉬워요.

phrases.en: Try supposing the exam is tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보다'를 붙여서 한번 상상해 본다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 보다' gives a feeling of trying out the idea.

phrases.en: If we suppose it rains, where should we go?
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각의 출발점을 정하고 다음 이야기를 이어 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sets a starting point for thinking and leads into what follows.

phrases.example: 만약 내일 비가 온다면 집에 있을 거예요.
phrases.en: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가정하다'보다 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 비슷한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar expression that is more common in everyday talk.

explain_en: You use it when you do not know whether something is true but think as if it were. It is close to '만약' and '-다면', but '가정하다' sets up the starting point of your thinking. The noun '가정' also means a household, so it is easy to confuse.

examples.en: I stopped for a moment at the fork while walking along the mountain path.

examples.ko: 저 갈림길을 지나서 오른쪽으로 가면 시장이 나와요.
examples.en: If you pass that fork and go right, you will reach the market.

examples.ko: 지도를 봐도 어느 갈림길이 맞는지 몰랐어요.
examples.en: Even with the map, I did not know which fork was the right one.
That choice was a turning point in my life.

examples.ko: 갈림길마다 표지판이 있어서 길을 잃지 않았어요.
examples.en: There was a sign at every fork, so I did not get lost.

examples.ko: 지금은 회사를 옮길지 말지 갈림길에 서 있어요.
examples.en: Right now I am at a crossroads about whether to change companies.

explain: 갈림길은 길이 둘로 갈라지는 곳이에요. 길이 만나는 모양을 정확히 말할 때는 '삼거리', '사거리'를 써요. '갈림길에 서다'처럼 인생의 중요한 선택 앞에서도 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 졸업을 앞두고 진로 갈림길에 서 있어요.
phrases.en: to stand at a crossroads
phrases.nuance_ko: 길이 아니라 인생의 중요한 선택을 앞두었다는 비유예요. 진로, 이직, 결혼 같은 큰 결정에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for facing an important life choice such as career, changing jobs, or marriage, not an actual road.

explain_en: 갈림길 is a spot where a road splits in two. When you need the exact shape of a junction, you say 삼거리 or 사거리. People also say 갈림길에 서다 when they face a big life decision.

examples.en: I tapped my card at the subway gate and went in.
I'll wait for my friend in front of the ticket gate.

examples.ko: 표가 없으면 개찰구를 통과할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Without a ticket, you can't get through the gate.
During rush hour every gate is crowded.
My card wouldn't register at the gate, and I panicked.
Strollers have to go through the wide gate.

explain: 지하철이나 기차역에서 표나 교통카드를 확인하고 지나가는 곳이에요. 표를 사는 곳은 '매표소'라고 해서 서로 짝이 돼요. 보통 '개찰구를 통과하다', '개찰구에서 찍다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: Once you pass through the gate, it's right at the platform.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표나 카드를 확인하고 안으로 들어갈 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for passing through after the ticket or card is checked.

phrases.en: Tap your transit card at the gate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 카드를 대는 동작을 말할 때 일상적으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday way to talk about tapping a card.

phrases.en: There's a staff member beside the ticket gate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위치를 알려 줄 때 '옆', '근처'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with words like 옆 or 근처 to give a location.

explain_en: It is the gate at a subway or train station where your ticket or transit card is checked. The place where you buy tickets is a '매표소', so the two go together. People say '개찰구를 통과하다' or '개찰구에서 찍다'.
